message.reasoning_content: Record a description update analyzing the kernel. Key risks: kernel doesn't clamp to e4m3 finite range (max ±448), no saturation of NaN/Inf, no subnormal handling (values < 2^-6 should round to subnormal grid step 2^-9, not binade-based step), tie rounding ties-away vs nearest-even ok, negative handling of floor(x/step+0.5) fine. Also exp2(e-3) where log2 near exact powers of 2 could misclassify due to fp error (e.g., ax slightly below a power of 2). Round-half ties within mantissa grid: rounding to nearest representable—kernel rounds to nearest multiple of step within binade, but boundary between binades: e.g. x just below 2^k rounds within lower binade fine, but x in upper part of binade near 2^k rounds to 2^k which is representable — fine. But rounding up may produce 1.0*2^{k+1} which is representable; ok. Subnormals: e4m3 subnormals step is 2^-9 (2^-6 * 2^-3); for ax < 2^-6, kernel computes e.g. e=-7, step=2^-10, which doesn't match subnormal spacing 2^-9 — so grid mismatch. Also out-of-range > 448 should saturate or become inf; contract says "nearest representable e4m3 value" — values beyond max aren't representable; tests likely compare to torch's float8_e4m3fn cast or expected semantics. Record.
